title: 음식 이름 소리대로: 떡볶이[떡뽀끼]
objective: By the end, you can read food names like 떡볶이, 국물 and 볶음밥 and say their real sounds, such as [떡뽀끼], [궁물] and [보끔밥].
summary: Read Korean food names the way Korean speakers actually say them, using four common sound-change rules.

task.title: Read food words aloud
task.line: Use the four rules in the box to find how each word really sounds.

words.meaning: tteokbokki (spicy stir-fried rice cakes); say [떡뽀끼], rules 1 and 2

words.exampleMeaning: I had rice cake soup for breakfast.
Shall we have noodles for lunch?

letters.as: Final consonant slides to the next syllable, like 'an apple' → 'a-napple'.
The second consonant turns tense with no puff of air, like 'k' in 'sky'.
ㄱ turns into 'ng' (as in 'sing'), and ㅂ into 'm', before n or m.
ㅎ joins the ㄱ or ㅂ before it and makes a strong, breathy k or p.

exercises: Choose the real sound: ① 국밥 → [국밥] / [국빱] ② 밥물 → [밤물] / [밥물] ③ 국을 → [국을] / [구글]
Write the real sound in [ ]: ① 밥은 ② 떡만 ③ 밥하고
Which rule (1–4) do you hear? ① 식당 [식땅] ② 라면을 [라며늘] ③ 국하고 [구카고]
Is the sound in [ ] right? Write O or X. If X, write the right sound: ① 떡집 [떡찝] ② 밥만 [밥만] ③ 떡을 [떠글]
Read aloud and write the sounds in [ ]: ① 밥을 먹어요. ② 떡하고 우유 주세요.
answers: ① 2 (tense sound) ② 1 (slides over) ③ 4 (ㅎ makes it strong)
① O ② X → [밤만] ③ O
